chennu13.composite: No formal per-patient rule stated. The one positive patient (P1) was reported on a conjunction: a significant 400-700 ms GFP cluster vs baseline for explicit targets, a significant TCT, a significant explicit > implicit cluster in 400-700 ms, and topographic correlation with the controls' P3b. Holm correction across 21 patients is reported for P1 only: 'robust enough to survive a Bonferroni-Holm (Holm, 1979) correction for multiple comparisons across the group of 21 patients' (p.457). No correction across the 2 windows x 3 conditions x contrasts per patient is stated.
chennu13.control_rate: 8/8 for the P3b to explicit targets (400-700 ms); P3a to explicit targets 5/8.
chennu13.control_source: CH13 p.454: 'In all healthy volunteers, explicit targets elicited a consistently significant P3b in the 400-700 ms window, and a P3a within the 100-400 ms in five of them.' n = 8 from p.451: '8 neurologically healthy adults'.
chennu13.k_source: NOT STATED as a count; k = 1. The paper describes one experimental run of 20 blocks per participant, recorded within a multi-day admission, and gives no number of EEG sessions per patient. CH13 (NeuroImage Clin 3:450-461) p.451: 'The experiment comprised of 20 blocks (lasting approx. 1.5 min each)'; p.452: 'Over a full experimental run, half the blocks had YES as the explicit target and the other half had NO'; p.451: 'Patients were admitted for 4-5 days as part of a comprehensive testing protocol that included the EEG task described below'.

columbia.composite: Patient positive if >= 1 recording has AUC > 0.5 and one-tailed permutation p < 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across that patient's recordings (1-8); no correction across patients. NEJM19 p. 2501: 'Of the 104 patients, 16 (15%) had cognitive–motor dissociation detected on at least one recording.' NEJM19-SA p. 8: 'we applied the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for FDR correction at the patient level.' [code] save_cmd_status.py l. 44: any(x.p_signif == True) per patient.
columbia.control_source: NEJM19 p. 2501: 'The healthy volunteers all had EEG evidence of brain activation in response to motor commands.' NEJM19-SA p. 8: 'All healthy volunteers fulfilled the CMD criteria for the motor command protocol set for patients (P < 0.05; median AUC 0.86 [0.73 - 0.91], ranging from 0.67 to 0.94).' Caveat NEJM19-SA p. 4: controls did real movement and only 3 right-hand blocks ('healthy volunteers showed real movement following the spoken commands'). EGB22 Results: 'Brain activation to motor commands was seen in all 14 healthy volunteers tested' (15 recorded; discrepancy unexplained).
columbia.k_source: DECISION 2026-10-14: reported as the k = 2 bracket. No single k is stated. NEJM19-SA p. 8 ('False discovery rate'): 'In between 1 and 8 recordings were obtained from individual patients.' Totals: 240 recordings in 104 patients (NEJM19-SA p. 9: 'Detection of EEG patterns ... was made in 31 (13%) of the patient recordings'; NEJM19-SA p. 13: '12 of the 240 recordings'; NEJM19 p. 2501: 'Of the 104 patients'). [derived] mean 240/104 = 2.31 recordings per patient; k = 2 is the integer nearest that mean and matches the 'k = 2 bracket' reading. Source: the Columbia protocol notes sections 4-5.

cornell.composite: Per paradigm per assessment (GF11 section 2.9, repeated CU18 p. 1408): positive = OM1 (TGT-significant difference contiguous over > 2 Hz in one run AND at least a trend in the same channel and frequency range in another run) AND OM2 (>= 1 TGT difference survives FDR 0.05 over all channels x frequencies with all runs combined); 'indeterminate' = OM1 only. Patient positive if positive on >= 1 paradigm (up to 4) in >= 1 assessment, no correction across paradigms or assessments. CU18 p. 1410: 'Twenty-one of 28 patients studied demonstrated a positive outcome for a minimum of one EEG paradigm, during at least one assessment.' Authors' caveat CU18 p. 1419: 'positive performance of one of the paradigms demonstrated here is not proposed as an evidentiary standard'.
cornell.control_rate: 15/15 (100%) positive on >= 1 paradigm (CU18); GF11: 4/4 on motor imagery
cornell.control_source: CU18 p. 1409: 'We observed EEG evidence of motor imagery task performance in all 15 healthy controls; 12 controls demonstrated a positive response to all paradigms tested, two controls demonstrated a positive response to three out of four paradigms tested, and one control subject demonstrated a positive response to two out of four paradigms tested.' Controls imagined; most patients also completed an actual-movement open/close-hand version, which controls did not (CU18 p. 1406). GF11 section 3.1 summary: HCs 'met the criteria for outcome measure 1 ... and outcome measure 2' (4 HCs analysed for motor; HC 5 motor data discarded, section 2.2).
cornell.k_source: CU18 p. 1406: 'In addition, we obtained longitudinal studies in six patients at two time points.' So 22 of 28 patients had 1 assessment and 6 had 2. [derived] 34 assessments / 28 patients = 1.21; k = 1 is the integer nearest the mean (same rule as columbia). Within an assessment, up to 4 paradigms: CU18 p. 1419: 'we tested multiple command-following paradigms in our subjects (four for most subjects reported here)'. Runs per paradigm: CU18 'multiple runs' (number NOT STATED); GF11 section 2.2: 'Subjects performed 2 to 4 runs for each task'.

cruse11.composite: Single assessment. CR11 p. 3: 'we used a test of whether the 99% and 99·9% binomial CIs for the estimates included chance (50%) to ascribe a significance level to each score' (binofit, Clopper-Pearson [ext]) AND 'We deemed the classification accuracy in the action period after each tone to be significantly greater than the classification accuracy in this baseline period if it was outside the binomial CIs for the baseline accuracy.' Positives reported at p < 0·01 or < 0·001 (p. 4 table). No correction across patients (CR13 proof p. 3).
cruse11.control_source: CR11 p. 4: 'Nine (75%) of the 12 healthy controls produced EEG data that could be classified significantly above chance (all p<0·01).' Null task, same page: 'no healthy control participant returned EEG responses that could be classified significant according to the commands (mean 51%, range 45–58%; all p>0·05)' (mind-wander instruction; 0/12).
cruse11.k_source: NOT STATED; k = 1. CR11 reports one accuracy per patient (Table, online-first PDF p. 4); the assessment is 4-8 blocks of each imagery type (p. 2: 'All patients completed at least four (range four to eight) blocks of each type of movement'). Patients were admitted 4-5 days for a separate protocol (p. 2) but the number of EEG sessions is not given. Multi-day testing appears only as a recommendation (p. 6): 'many testing sessions for several days with this EEG technique will provide each patient with an increased opportunity to show their covert awareness'.

cruse12p.composite: Two comparisons (left-hand vs rest, right-hand vs rest), each a max-over-time label permutation (1000), threshold '.05/2 (.025, one-tailed)' (Methods, single-trial classification). Positive if either comparison is significant: implied by the threshold and by reporting 'at least one comparison' for controls; an explicit 'any' rule is NOT STATED. Patient result: 'Only the classification between left-hand and rest was significantly above chance' (Results).
cruse12p.control_source: CR12P Results, Single-trial Analyses: 'Five of the six healthy participants returned significantly above chance classification in at least one comparison (median 66.5%, range 60–80%; see Table 2). Conversely, when instructed to mind-wander and not to the follow the commands, no healthy controls returned significant classification in any comparison (median 57%, range 52–63%).' Controls performed real hand squeezes ('they rapidly squeezed their hands into a fist four times', Methods 'Procedure').
cruse12p.k_source: One assessment of one patient. CR12P (PMC3503880) Methods 'Procedure': 'The patient completed five blocks during the assessment, for a total of 180 trials'. Controls: one follow run and one mind-wander run each ('In a separate run, control participants also listened to the same task but were instructed simply to mind-wander').

dubois.composite: DB26 Methods 'Phase I (Sessions 1–2)': 'Participants advanced to the next phase when DA exceeded 70% or when task-related DAs were statistically greater than baseline (one-tailed paired t-test, α = 0.05).' Reported as Abstract: 'Significant MI-BCI decoding accuracy (DA) is achieved by 73.8% of patients' = Results: 'N = 33, 73.8% of patients passed assessment' [derived 31/42]. Per run: best of up to 84 FBCSP-MuI configurations [derived], peak DA 0.4-7 s vs peak of the -1 to 0 s baseline, one-tailed paired t-test across 6 CV folds; a 100-label permutation is also run but its role in the call is NOT STATED. No correction across runs, sessions or configurations stated.
dubois.control_source: DB26 Results, first paragraph: 'Following Phase I (assessment), 8 of 14 UWS, 13 of 17 MCS, 10 of 11 LIS patients, and both AB participants progressed to Phase II'. Benchmarks only (Methods: 'Two able-bodied males (aged 20 and 23) were included as benchmarks'); no sham or no-command control.
dubois.k_source: DECISION 2026-10-14: k = 2 under the published Phase I pass rule (sessions 1-2) for A1(b); the 12-session best-of-k on pDoC stays descriptive. The published call (Phase I pass) uses sessions 1-2. DB26 (PMC13272656) Methods heading '#### Phase I (Sessions 1–2)'; Table 1: 'Phase I (Assessment paradigm) Session 1: A1, F(PN); Session 2: A2, T, F(PN)' [derived: up to 5 Phase-I runs: 2 Assessment, 1 Training, 2 Feedback]. Which Phase-I runs count toward the pass rule: NOT STATED. Whole study: 'Participants who advanced completed 4–13 sessions, each comprising 1–5 runs' (Methods, Experimental paradigm); Table 1 lists sessions 1-12.

edlow17.composite: Per paradigm: 'We considered a patient to have a positive EEG response if P < 0.05' (p. 2403; one-sided, 500 label permutations, p = count/500). CMD (Table 2 legend, p. 2406): 'CMD is defined by functional MRI or EEG evidence of command-following on the active motor imagery task despite absence of language function on behavioural evaluation.' For the EEG motor-imagery pipeline alone: one test per patient.
edlow17.control_source: ED17 p. 2406: 'Twelve of 16 healthy subjects had EEG responses to motor imagery [75.0% (95% CI: 47.6–92.7%)].' ED17-S Table 3 (p. 16) per-control motor-imagery EEG p-values: p < 0.05 in C1, C2, C3 (0.044), C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10, C11, C13, C16; not in C4 0.114, C12 0.112, C14 0.058, C15 0.106. Note: an earlier note cited 'Edlow 2017 MI 68.8-75%'; ED17 states only 75.0% (11/16 = 68.8% [derived] does not appear in ED17 or ED17-S).
edlow17.k_source: NOT STATED explicitly; k = 1. ED17 describes one EEG per patient scheduled against the fMRI: p. 2404: 'EEG was performed within 24 h of functional MRI in 11 patients. However, scheduling and ICU issues ... led to an increased time between the two assessments for five patients'. Repeat EEG sessions are not described.

gibson16.composite: Per patient, each effect is called by a FieldTrip cluster-mass permutation test (1000 randomisations, 50-750 ms; tails and cluster alpha NOT STATED): P3a = deviant vs standard; P3b (top-down, the command-following analogue) = target vs non-target wrist. No correction across the SSEP, P3a and P3b tests is stated. The awareness reference standard is an any-of-three rule (p.11): 'A patient was considered to have evidence of such awareness if they demonstrated evidence of command following in any one of the three non-EEG assessments'.
gibson16.control_source: GIB16 AAM p.9: 'this ERP effect was evident for healthy volunteers at the group level (n=15) and at the single-subject level, albeit with a hit-rate of 67%'; p.13: 'P3b responses in the current work were detected from only 67% (10/15) of the healthy volunteers'; p.9: bottom-up effects in 'all of the healthy volunteers (n=15; Figure 3)'; p.9: 'A steady-state evoked potential was detected in the EEG data of all patients (n=14) and all healthy volunteers (n=15)'.
gibson16.k_source: One EEG assessment per patient in the primary analysis; k = 1. A repeat was done for 4/14 patients and reported separately as replication. GIB16 author accepted manuscript ('Page n of 42' header) p.6: 'Patients VS4, MCS3, and EMCS1 participated in second assessments with the somatosensory selective attention task and the CRS-R. These assessments occurred from 2- to 3.5-months following their initial participation. Patient VS6 completed a second assessment with all paradigms (CRS-R, fMRI, and EEG) 22-months after her initial assessment.' Both VS6 observations were counted once in the association test (p.11: 'p=.0047 if the two observations of Patient VS6 are not included').

mbmi.composite: Per run: CV accuracy above a binomial chance bound; repeat the run if below (OR17). GU17 'LIS participants procedure': communication attempted if MI accuracy 'higher than 63.19% (95% confidence interval for 60 trials using a binomial test)'. CH18 section 2.5: 'A differentiated EEG response ... was defined as a classification accuracy exceeding the chance threshold calculated based on a binomial distribution ... p < .05 (... n = 60 for MoI ...)'. OR17: 'An accuracy level above that line means that the result is statistically significant (alpha <0.05)' (Clopper-Pearson 95% limit). Patient-level aggregation across runs (>= 1 run vs best run): NOT STATED explicitly for MI; which time point of the 0.5-s accuracy course is the run's value: NOT STATED.
mbmi.control_rate: GU17: 3/3 healthy subjects (5/6 regular runs >= 63.19% by Table 3); CH18: 2/10 (20%)
mbmi.control_source: GU17 Table 3 (PMC5418541, 3 healthy subjects S1-S3) MI regular runs: Run 1 70/71/78%, Run 2 90/67/62%; sham 55/50/59%. GU17 text: 'For the MI approach, accuracy is above the significance threshold (63.19%) during the two regular runs, and near chance level (below the significance level) for the sham run.' Discrepancy: S3 Run 2 = 62% < 63.19%. CH18 section 3.3.3 (PMC6045427, ICU, mindBEAGLE): 'only 2 of 10 HS showed a differentiated response with MI (HS Se = 20%).' CH18 motor action version: 'Five of the eight HS who completed MoA had differentiated responses (Se = 62.5%)' (section 3.3.4).
mbmi.k_source: DECISION 2026-10-14 (rule: stated value, else k = 1): k = 1 primary; k = 2 sensitivity (one repeat run if the first fails). No number is stated as a digit. OR17 (JoVE 2017, PMC5613801, Protocol step 6 'MI assessment'): 'If the accuracy level is below the significance level, repeat the run. If the accuracy remains below this significance level, then reliable communication is unlikely, at least with that paradigm and recording session.' Read as one assessment run plus one repeat if it fails, so k = 2 per session. If a numeric statement is required, k = 1 (NOT STATED numerically). Runs actually reported: GU17 Table 4 (60-instruction MI) one MI run per patient except P12 (two rows: 42%, 74%); CH18 section 2.3.5: 'When time allowed ..., a second run was administered immediately after the first one, using classifiers built during the first session' (CH18 section 3.3.4: 'A second session was partly administered in nine patients (9 AEP, 8 VTP2, 3 VTP3, 7 MoI, 6 MoA)'). GU17/CH18 report one session per patient.

mbvt.composite: Any run positive, no multiplicity correction stated. GUG18 Abstract: 'the VT2 or VT3 accuracy was above the significance threshold of 23% for at least one run'; Methods: 'A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment ... 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test' (n behind the 23% bound NOT STATED). SPA18 Abstract: 'task following in one or both paradigms'. MUR20 uses the best run: 'Every patient achieved at least 60% accuracy at least once, which indicates successful command following' (Abstract). ANN18: VT2 > 70% gate before VT3.
mbvt.control_rate: 3/3 healthy above the 23% threshold in every regular VT2 and VT3 run [derived from the stated range 60-100%; not stated as a detection rate]. Sham runs: 1/3 VT2 shams above 23% (25%), 0/3 VT3 shams [derived]. SPA18: 6 healthy controls, rate NOT STATED ('expected results').
mbvt.control_source: GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC full text, Results 'Healthy controls and sham results' and Table 3; no printed pages accessible): 'For the two EP-based approaches (VT2 and VT3), accuracy is between 60 and 100% in regular runs, and 0 to 25% for sham runs.' Table 3 sham VT2 = 0, 25, 10; sham VT3 = 0, 10, 10. SPA18 Abstract (p.1130): 'The BCI system also yielded the expected results with healthy controls.'
mbvt.k_source: Runs per session as published for the mindBEAGLE command-following assessment = 2 (one VT2 + one VT3). SPA18 Abstract (Clin Neurophysiol 2018;129:p.1130): 'Thirteen UWS patients and six healthy controls each participated in two experimental runs'. GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC full text, Results; no printed pages accessible): 'Eleven patients were seen for one or two runs in 1 day. The remaining patient (UWS1) was assessed for 2 runs per days on 4 different days' and 'between 1 and 4 runs for VT2, 1-7 runs for VT3' per patient across sessions. Alternatives for sensitivity: MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294, Methods 'Paradigm'): 'For patients P1-P10, each session consisted of 12 VT3 runs. For patients P11-P20, each session consisted of 8 VT3 runs', over 10 sessions (80-120 runs per patient); ANN18 (Discussion): 'every patient was assessed only once with the P3 system' (VT2, plus VT3 only if VT2 > 70%).

sokoliuk21.composite: No per-patient call rule in Methods. The predictor is continuous: phrase- and sentence-rate ITPC, averaged across electrodes, correlated with GOSE. Added later only, p.655: 'a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis of our sentence / phrase-level ITPC data indicates 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity ... (GOSE > = 3; threshold = 0.116 ...)'. Passive paradigm, no command.
sokoliuk21.control_rate: NOT STATED (SOK21 recruited no healthy controls; Fig 1C shows only a group-average spectrum of 20 healthy participants from a separate study, with no per-subject detection rate).
sokoliuk21.control_source: SOK21 p.649, Figure 1 legend: '(C) This panel shows average cortical tracking over 20 healthy, comprehending participants (these data are taken from our recent study ... Sokoliuk et al. [2020] bioRxiv)'. The companion SOK21b (Front Hum Neurosci 15:702768, n = 72) reports group-level tracking only; single-subject rate NOT STATED.
sokoliuk21.k_source: One EEG recording per patient; the count is NOT STATED explicitly, so k = 1. SOK21 (Ann Neurol 89:646-656) p.647: '21 patients met all inclusion/exclusion criteria at the time of EEG, between 48 hours and 7 days after sedation hold'. Limitation, p.655: 'multiple applications of this paradigm per patient could minimize potential confounding influences of patient arousal'.
